messages.subject: Re: daply and POSIXct
parts:
I have to admit this is rather curious.

My first thought was to use apply(); since all of the variables in the
dates object are character, this should have been easy.

mkPOSIX1 <- function(r)
as.POSIXct(paste(paste(r, collapse = '/'), '12/00/00', sep = '/'),
format = '%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M/%s',
origin = '1970-01-01 00:00:00',
tz='UTC')
> apply(dates, 1, mkPOSIX1)
1 2 3 4 5
883656000 883742400 883828800 883915200 884001600

# Numeric codes?? Sigh.
as.POSIXct(apply(dates, 1, mkPOSIX1), origin = '1970-01-01 00:00:00',
tz = 'UTC')

1 2 3
"1998-01-01 12:00:00 UTC" "1998-01-02 12:00:00 UTC" "1998-01-03 12:00:00 UTC"
4 5
"1998-01-04 12:00:00 UTC" "1998-01-05 12:00:00 UTC"

This is easy to rewrite as a matrix, so I'll let it go. If one applies
the mkPOSIX1 function to an individual row, it works:

> mkPOSIX1(dates[1, ])
[1] "1998-01-01 12:00:00 UTC"

The second thought was..."OK, I'll use mdply on it instead. Hah!"
Close, but no cigar...

mkPOSIX <- function(year, month, day)
as.POSIXct(paste(paste(c(year, month, day), collapse = '/'),
'12/00/00', sep = '/'),
format = '%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M/%s',
origin = '1970-01-01 00:00:00',
tz='UTC')

> mdply(dates, mkPOSIX)
year month day V1
1 1998 01 01 1998-01-01 04:00:00
2 1998 01 02 1998-01-02 04:00:00
3 1998 01 03 1998-01-03 04:00:00
4 1998 01 04 1998-01-04 04:00:00
5 1998 01 05 1998-01-05 04:00:00

4AM??? I changed the origin of the time component a few times (12 PM,
8 AM, 4 AM) and it kept returning the same result. I'm guessing it's
returning the local time zone (in my case PT) rather than UTC.

Thought three: try the lubridate package....

mkPOSIX2 <- function(year, month, day) {
require('lubridate')
ymd(paste(c(year, month, day), collapse = '/')) + hours(12)
}

mkPOSIX2(2002, 1, 4)
[1] "2002-01-04 12:00:00 UTC" # looks promising...

> mdply(dates, mkPOSIX2)
year month day V1
1 1998 01 01 1998-01-01 04:00:00
2 1998 01 02 1998-01-02 04:00:00
3 1998 01 03 1998-01-03 04:00:00
4 1998 01 04 1998-01-04 04:00:00
5 1998 01 05 1998-01-05 04:00:00

Uncle! If someone has a quick explanation/fix for this, I'm all ears.

Dennis

parts:
Thanks David and Dennis-

My main issues is that it seems like a tremendous waste to create a list (e.g. a dataframe) and then strip it down to a vector (esp when the number of dates is 10k+). Quite basically, I want to use plyr with .parallel=TRUE, put dataframe in, and get a vector of POSIXct class out. Is this unreasonable?

Perhaps naively, i think of a vector as a 1-d array and I also believe that I should be able to recover a 1-d array from and n-d array - this goes on all the time.  But *aply is choking on POSIXct even when I boil it down to a 1-d problem. 

## it's easy enough to convert the dates dataframe to a vector with an intermediate step
dates.str <- c("1998/01/01", "1998/01/02", "1998/01/03", "1998/01/04", "1998/01/05")

## gives same error as before
mk.POSIXct <-
 function(r) as.POSIXct(paste(r,'12/00/00',sep='/'),
format='%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M/%s', tz='UTC')

POSIXct.vector <- aaply( dates.str, 1, mk.POSIXct )

##but this works just fine but seems ludicrous.
mk.POSIXct <-
 function(r) as.numeric(as.POSIXct(paste(r,'12/00/00',sep='/'),
                        format='%Y/%m/%d/%H/%M/%s', tz='UTC'))
POSIXct.vector <- as.POSIXct(aaply( dates.str, 1, mk.POSIXct ),origin = '1970-01-01 00:00:00')

James
